title: Ephemeral build workers, dependency pin audit, and transparent cache priming
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Background: Our fleet of long-lived CI runners and opaque build caches contributes to flakiness, non-reproducible artifacts, and high maintenance cost when we bump base images or toolchains. This ticket groups three coordinated efforts: 1) introduce ephemeral build workers (short-lived, immutable runner images) to reduce stateful cache divergence; 2) run a dependency pinning audit across our monorepo to identify semver drift and risky transitive deps; 3) implement a transparent cache priming mechanism so cache miss behavior is observable and we can pre-warm critical layers for common PR patterns. Goals: reduce flaky builds by 40% in the next quarter, cut median build time for fast-path PRs by 20%, and create a reproducible-build checklist for releases.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ephemeral worker pool deployed to CI (k8s job-based or cloud runners) with documented rollout steps and automated image rotation.
- Dependency audit report produced listing top 50 third-party deps by occurrence and transitive version conflicts, with a remediation backlog created.
- Cache priming pipeline that can pre-populate our CAS for the 10 most common Docker layers and node/python wheel sets prior to CI runs.
- Observability: build cache hit/miss dashboard with per-repo breakdown and alert when hit-rate drops >10%.
- No more than 2% increase in CI infra cost during canary; and a plan to recover costs via smarter caching/packaging.
implementation_notes:
Workstreams:
1) Ephemeral workers
  - Create minimal immutable runner images (distroless base + preinstalled build tools). Image variant matrix: node, python, go, bazel-shim. Use image tags with commit hash and TTL-based rotation.
  - Migrate a subset of repositories (infra/*, sdk/*) to ephemeral runners behind a feature flag.
  - Provide fallbacks and graceful retry to existing pool for first 2 weeks.
2) Dependency pin audit
  - Use 'renovate' dry-run across monorepo, capture semver mismatches, and extract transitive graph for top offenders.
  - Run security/compat checks (SNYK / OSV) and annotate PRs with suggested pins or upgrades.
3) Transparent cache priming
  - Implement a priming job that pushes critical Docker layers and pip/npms to our internal CAS and registry. Buildkit cache exporter -> remote cache.
  - Add instrumentation in CI to annotate each job with cache-source headers and surface in the Console.
Implementation decisions made:
  - Prefer immutable ephemeral images instead of ephemeral containers on heavy mutable hosts to simplify rollbacks.
  - Use existing image registry and ACR/GCR lifecycle rules for TTL rather than building a new garbage collector.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Prep (this ticket)
  - Build ephemeral images and test locally. Create canary repos list.
Phase 1: Canary (2 weeks)
  - Route 10% of PRs in canary repos to ephemeral workers. Monitor failures, cache hits, infra cost.
Phase 2: Expand (4 weeks)
  - Increase to 50% and run dependency remediation PRs in parallel.
Phase 3: Full (by release)
  - Replace default worker pool; enable cache priming for all PRs. Decommission legacy long-lived runners gradually.
metrics:
- Build flakiness rate (flake builds / total builds) — baseline 6% -> target <=3.6%.
- Median PR build latency (fast-path) — baseline 9m -> target 7.2m.
- Cache hit rate for primary layer set — baseline 62% -> target >=80%.
- Number of dependency semver conflicts detected and remediated.
- CI infra cost delta (USD/month) during canary.
risks:
- Ephemeral images missing edge-case tool (native client builds) causing subtle failures — mitigation: allow on-demand mount of legacy tool cache and run compatibility tests.
- Cache priming could mask dependency drift leading to surprise production issues — mitigation: pair priming with verifiable checksums and reproducible artifact signing.
- Developers may see transient latency increases during rollout — mitigation: dev communication, opt-in flags for noisy repos.

2025-02-05 - Jonah Park: Canary started for infra/* repos. First week stats: cache hit-rate increased from 60% -> 73% for canary runs; two flakes attributable to missing apt packages in the ephemeral image (fixed and new image pushed).
2025-02-14 - Security team note: ran OSV scan against pinned-deps; 2 medium severity transitive vulns flagged — creating remediation PRs in sprint backlog.
2025-02-20 - Jonah Park: Cost telemetry shows +1.8% infra spend in canary. Within threshold. Next: widen canary to sdk/* and core-service/* and start automated priming for top-10 layers.
